text:
Kai: heads up — saw a bunch of microbatch churn after last kernel selector tweak this morning, 99th latency spiking + KV hit rate drop. anyone else seeing it?
Sara: saw it, correlates with the 03:12 deploy. perf dashboard shows small batches forming more often.
Mikko: interesting, I also pulled a flame and noticed more context-switching in the runner threads. could be queue batching thresholds bouncing.
Kai: attaching quick repro logs below — happens on p-serve-7 under medium load (20-30 rps).
deploy-bot: deploy v2026.03.12-kernel-opt applied to p-serve-7 at 03:12:45 UTC
Sara: raw tail of request log: `2026-03-12T03:15:12Z svc:microbatch formed size=2 delay_ms=1.4 token_budget=16 kernel=fast-attn-v2` repeated a lot.
Mikko: that token_budget 16 is suspect for this workload (we usually target 24-40). kernel fast-attn-v2 has slightly higher per-token latency, so the runtime probably reduced batch target to keep latency SLO, ending up with more tiny batches.
Anya: from KV perspective, cache hit ratio dropped from 93% -> 78% around the same time. small batches reduce prefix cache reuse.
Kai: TL;DR: kernel selector is preferring fast-attn-v2 which increases per-token time; coalesce heuristics then shrink batches to hit latency targets -> more churn -> worse KV hit -> higher tail. vicious cycle.
Sara: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) bump token_budget_target to 32 for medium tier, 2) raise microbatch_hold_ms from 1 -> 2 (to allow slightly larger assemblies), 3) introduce jitter floor: coalesce_jitter_ms min 0.5.
Mikko: agree for rollback window. Also propose an affinity tweak: prefer kernel=fast-attn-v1 for seq_len<128 when throughput is >15rps. quick patch:
```yaml
runtime:
  batching:
    token_budget_target: 32
    microbatch_hold_ms: 2.0
    coalesce_jitter_ms: { min: 0.5, pct: 0.12 }
  kernel_affinity:
    - condition: "seq_len < 128 and qps > 15"
      prefer: fast-attn-v1
```
Sara: ran a local sim with that config on 30k simulated reqs — 95th/99th improved ~12%/18%, KV hit recovered to ~90%.
Kai: good. any risk to throughput or cost from higher token_budget_target?
Mikko: small bump in token consolidation reduces kernel invocations per token, should reduce GPU kernel overhead. might increase memory pressure for extreme tokens, but within pool limits.
Anya: note: we should also add a KV eviction metric breakpoint — if hit ratio falls below 85% we should auto-relax hold_ms up to 5ms temporarily.
Sara: agreed. add a simple hysteresis so we don't oscillate. e.g., if KV_hit < 85% for 30s -> microbatch_hold_ms += 1ms, revert after 2m stable.
Kai: can someone open a quick PR with the runtime defaults + roll forward to canary? want to watch p-serve-7 and p-serve-9.
Mikko: I'll draft the PR and include the sim results + flame. tagging @ops for canary rollout window.
deploy-bot: canary job scheduled for p-serve-7 at 04:08 UTC (10% traffic).
Anya: for postmortem data capture: please enable detailed KV sampling for the canary (3x sampling rate) and keep per-request batch_size and kernel labels.
Sara: noted. I'll add dashboard panels: batch_size distribution, token_budget vs latency, KV_hit by kernel.
Kai: thanks team — timeline: PR in next 30m, canary 04:08, monitor 30m, revert if 99th > baseline + 15%.
Mikko: one more thought: we should instrument and log when kernel selector triggers fallback. that will help detect when affinity rules flip frequently.
Sara: adding a short log line: `kernel_affinity: reason=[fast-path|fallback] selected=...`
Kai: perfect. after canary we'll decide if permanent default change or adjust selector thresholds.
Anya: adding an action item: write an automated regression test that fuzzes seq_len / qps and validates KV_hit >= 88% at target latency.
Kai: cool. Anyone object? otherwise I'll proceed with PR review and merge after green CI. :thumbsup:
Mikko: +1
Sara: +1
Anya: +1
Kai: (closing) moving to #eng-runtime sync notes.
